title: Check, checkmate and stalemate
outcomes: Gets out of check in one of the three ways, and sees when a way is impossible
Tells check, checkmate and stalemate apart
Gives mate without stalemating by accident

steps.text: When your king is attacked it is in **check**. You must fix it at once, in one of three ways: **move** the king, **block** the attack with a piece, or **capture** the piece that gives check. You may never make a move that leaves your own king in check.

steps.caption: White is in check. The king can step away, the bishop can block, or the rook can capture.

steps.text: If there is **no** way out of check, it is **checkmate**: the game ends and the player in check loses. If the player to move is **not** in check but has no legal move, it is **stalemate**: the game is a draw. The two look alike, but the results are opposite.

steps.caption: The rook checks along the back rank (the row where the pieces start). The king's own pawns block its escape. Checkmate.

steps.title: One square, opposite results
steps.prompt: The white queen moves from f8 to f7, one square down. Predict first: is the result still checkmate?
In the last four questions you were not told what to look for. How sure were you of each answer? (low / medium / high)
